corrections.what_happened: The laptop's lid was closed while the answers were being made. Two answer calls were under way, one after the other. Each was cut as a timeout when the laptop woke, although its reply had come back, and was asked again. The second reply is the answer that was kept and judged. No answer, context or score is changed by this correction: only times.

rule.text:
A try of a model call is one the machine slept under when all three hold:
  1. it ended as a timeout;
  2. it lasted longer than its own timeout (a call that is running is cut at its timeout, so a
     longer one was not running the whole time);
  3. the low-power time the machine itself logged inside the try's start and end is at least the
     try's overrun past its timeout.
The seconds recorded for such a try are taken out of the three sums they went into: the row's
generator.time_s and generator.retry_s, the row's timing.wall_s, and the wall_s of that start in
the run manifest. What those sums hold afterwards: the try that answered, the pause the harness
waits before it tries again, and the harness's own overhead. The slept try's own share of awake
seconds, in which its reply came back, cannot be told apart from the sleep by the run's clock and
goes out with it.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: generator.attempts is 2 and generator.calls is 1 in these rows: two requests were made and paid for, one answer was kept.
The tokens of the discarded reply are listed under slept_tries. They are not part of the row's token counts, which are those of the try that answered.
The try that answered read the prompt from the cache the first try had written (generator.cached_input_tokens), which no other row of this run does.
started_at, finished_at and answered_at are clock times and have the sleep between them.

judge_calls_with_logged_low_power_time_i.note: No change is made to these. Whether the call was held while the machine was in this state is not known from the record, so its seconds stand as recorded.

low_power_intervals_the_machine_logged.what: Modern Standby: Reason: Austerity Battery Drain Budget Exceeded.
Modern Standby: Reason: Sleep, Hibernate, or Shutdown.

corrections.what_happened: The row's retrieval and build_stats each held one sum, all zero, in the form the arms cannot share without adding two models together.

rule.text:
1. A row's retrieval is its own call records summed per model (harness.capture.usage_by_model),
     the answer call left out. The answer call is the record whose system text is the harness's
     answer instruction; it is marked role: answer, and its tokens must be the generator's.
  2. The entries must hold what the row recorded: the same calls, tokens in, tokens out and cached
     tokens in all.
  3. artefact_v4 only: search_time_s loses the embedder's seconds (lock_wait_s + encode_s of the
     row's embed records) and the seconds of the first-call tries that did not answer (the chat
     entry's retry_s).
  4. build_stats gets one entry per model, from the run's own manifest: lucene none; vector the
     embedder, from its build_stats and the stored file's cost note; artefact_v4 from
     index.build_cost (artefact_v4.build_stats_from_cost).
  5. artefact_v4 only: the graph block takes the graph's last build record and the graph counted
     now (orchestrator.graph_census), after a check that the graph holds now what the run counted
     at its start.
  6. artefact_v4 only: the sha256 of the code files (meta.provenance.source_sha256) and of the
     build cost file (index.build_cost_file_sha256) become those of the commit's files, their
     line ends as git holds them (LF), after a check that each recorded value is the commit's
     file with the Windows line ends the checkout wrote.

not_changed_and_worth_knowing: No answer, context, id, score or judge call is changed; the call records are changed only by the answer call's role.

A retrieval entry's seconds are the tries' and the embedder's own seconds from the call records. The sum the arm recorded held the seconds around each call, so the entries hold a little less; that rest is the arm's own work, in timing.wall_s.
timing.wall_s and the stamps are unchanged. The sleep correction before this one stands as it was.
